title: Stable nonarchimedean valued fields
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] with a real-valued multiplicative nonarchimedean absolute value. For each finite-dimensional field extension $E/k$, equip $E$ with the minimal-polynomial spectral norm $s_{E/k}$ of [lem-trf-incomplete-spectral-algebra-norm]. Call $k$ stable if every such $E/k$ has a $k$-basis $v_1,\ldots,v_n$, with $n=\dim_k E$, such that $$s_{E/k}\left(\sum_{i=1}^n a_iv_i\right)=\max_{1\le i\le n}|a_i|s_{E/k}(v_i)\quad(a_i\in k).$$ Thus stable means that every finite extension with its spectral norm is a cartesian normed vector space; no completeness or separability is imposed on $k$ or $E/k$.

source.place: Definition 3.6.1/1 and its following paragraph, printed p.156 (scan PDF p.164); cartesian means existence of the orthogonal basis displayed here. Primary scan read 2026-10-24.

It defines a stable field: k carries a real-valued nonarchimedean absolute value, and every finite extension E/k has a basis that is orthogonal for the minimal-polynomial spectral norm s_{E/k}, i.e. s(Σa_i v_i) = max|a_i| s(v_i). This agrees with BGR Def. 3.6.1/1 (cartesian in the sense of 2.4.1/1, spectral norm as in 3.2.1). BGR is not in literature/, so I could not reread the page locally; I checked the definition against BGR's formulation as I know it, and the worker cites the online scan and flags it WANTED. Edge cases checked: E=k with basis (1); algebraically closed k, the case used in step 2 of lem-trf-tate-fraction-orthogonal-spectral-norm; trivial absolute value (s=1 off 0, every basis orthogonal); Q_p(√p) with basis (1,√p); n≥1 so the max is never empty. rg -L over the DAG finds only the users tate-gauss-fraction-stability and tate-fraction-orthogonal-spectral-norm. lean.statement: def IsStableNonarchimedeanField (K : Type u) [NormedField K] [IsUltrametricDist K] : Prop

reviewed_lean.note: IsStableNonarchimedeanField (K:Type u)[NormedField K][IsUltrametricDist K] = ∀ finite field ext E:Type (max u v), ∃ basis indexed by Fin (finrank K E) with spectralNorm K E (∑ a i • b i) = ⨆ i, ‖a i‖·spectralNorm K E (b i). Matches the node and BGR Def. 3.6.1/1 (cartesian = has an orthogonal basis for the spectral norm), checked from knowledge: the BGR PDF is not in literature/ and the download was blocked. Uses the dependency's own spectralNorm (minpoly spectral value); adds no completeness, separability or nontriviality assumption. The index is never empty, so ⨆ = max. Edge cases E=K, trivial absolute value and n=0 checked. The body-only universe v is harmless: finite extensions transport to Type u and spectralNorm is invariant under algebra isomorphism, so the predicate is the same for every v (advisory for citers).
